stories.title: US intelligence chief defends Trump’s comments calling Putin his ‘friend’
stories.summary: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton says Trump's comments were 'entirely appropriate' in context of summit.
stories.detail: Jay Clayton was pressed on Trump’s characterization of Putin during media appearances on Sunday Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, said he trusts Donald Trump “completely” after the US president called Vladimir Putin “a friend” during their recent meeting in China. Clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. After a backlash at home and aboard, Trump doubled down on Saturday and posted a photo of himself and Putin shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.”

details.summary: US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton says Trump's comments were 'entirely appropriate' in context of summit.

Kurt Volker, former U.S. Ambassador to NATO, tells CBC's Rosemary Barton that it’s 'appalling' to hear U.S. President Donald Trump double down on calling Russian President Vladimir Putin his 'friend.'

stories.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Libya's eastern government says a sunken warship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia.
stories.detail: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.

details.summary: Libya's eastern government says a sunken warship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia.

stories.title: UN-affiliated athlete swims in dangerous Strait of Hormuz to highlight Iran war's impact on wildlife
stories.summary: Lewis Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days last week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how Iran war threatens the area's habitat and wildlife.
stories.detail: UN patron Lewis Pugh saw ships ablaze and fighter jets overhead during three-day swim as Iran conflict continues A British endurance swimmer has completed a three-day swim through the strait of Hormuz to highlight the environmental cost of the Iran war. Lewis Pugh, a UN patron of the oceans, swam the 9.3-mile (15km) length of the waterway, which is a key route for oil shipments from the Middle East.
